The Prince William County Circuit Court was established in 1892, as part of a statewide reorganization of Virginia's judicial system. It replaced the county court, which had been the primary court of general jurisdiction in Prince William County since the colonial era. The circuit court initially had only one judge, but additional judges were added as the county's population grew.

Jurisdiction of the Prince William County Circuit Court

The Prince William County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases within the county. This includes:

  • Civil Cases: The circuit court has jurisdiction over civil cases involving claims of more than $25,000. This includes contract disputes, personal injury claims, and property disputes, among others.
  • Criminal Cases: The circuit court has jurisdiction over all felony cases and certain misdemeanor cases. This includes cases involving drug offenses, property crimes, and violent crimes, among others.
  • Appeals: The circuit court also has jurisdiction to hear appeals from lower courts within the county, including the general district court and juvenile and domestic relations district court.

Structure of the Prince William County Circuit Court

The Prince William County Circuit Court is led by a chief judge and several associate judges, who are appointed by the Virginia General Assembly. The court also has a clerk's office, which is responsible for maintaining court records and providing administrative support to the judges.

Potter, and William D. Hamblen. The judges are elected to eight-year terms, and their duties include presiding over court hearings, issuing orders and opinions, and making rulings on legal disputes.

Once a case is filed, the court will schedule a hearing. The date and time of the hearing will be provided to all parties involved. At the hearing, both sides will present their arguments and evidence, and the judge will make a ruling.

Appeals

If a party is not satisfied with the outcome of a case in the Prince William County Circuit Court, they may file an appeal. Appeals are heard by the Virginia Court of Appeals or the Virginia Supreme Court, depending on the type of case.
